prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2010 — “A Future Fair for All” (summary)

Core aim: Rebuild the economy, protect and reform frontline public services, strengthen society and communities, and renew politics for a fairer future.

Economy and public finances
- Secure the recovery by avoiding immediate 2010–11 cuts; more than halve the deficit in four years via growth, fair taxes and lower‑priority cuts.
- “Tough choices”: £15bn efficiency in 2010–11; £20bn/year by 2012–13 from operational savings; 1% cap on public‑sector pay rises (2011–13); public‑sector pension reforms; £20bn asset sales.
- Fair tax changes: 50p rate over £150k; reduced pension relief for the best‑off; 1p NI rise (from 2011, protecting incomes under £20k); bonus tax.
- Banking reform: tougher capital and “living wills”; global levy; constrain risky pay; boost competition and mutuals.
- Industrial strategy: UK Finance for Growth (£4bn), patent box, R&D credits; one million skilled jobs in green, digital, life sciences and advanced manufacturing.
- Infrastructure: High Speed Rail, Crossrail, rail electrification; Green Investment Bank; universal broadband (superfast rollout funded by landline levy); 100,000 EV charge points.

Work, welfare, and prosperity
- Job guarantees: Future Jobs Fund (200,000 jobs); mandatory job/training after six months for young people; guaranteed work after two years unemployed.
- Make work pay: Minimum wage to rise at least with average earnings; £40/week Better Off in Work guarantee; apprenticeships expansion; Skills Accounts.
- Housing: Two‑year stamp duty holiday for first‑time buyers up to £250k (funded by 5% rate over £1m); new affordable homes; protect from repossessions; council house building reforms.
- Consumer finance: People’s Bank at the Post Office; universal right to a basic bank account; clamp down on high‑cost lending; stronger consumer regulation.
- Saving: ISAs uplifted; Savings Gateway; protect Child Trust Fund; matched savings for young adults.

Education
- Protect frontline spending on Sure Start, childcare, schools, 16–19.
- Early years: expand free nursery places (age 2) and 15 hours for 3–4s.
- Schools: 3Rs guarantee with one‑to‑one/small‑group tuition; parental power to trigger leadership change; build up to 1,000 accredited school groups; fair admissions; local pupil premium; SEN focus.
- Secondary/skills: personal tutors; diplomas; Building Schools for the Future; participation to 18; major growth in advanced apprenticeships; widen HE access; funding review (Browne).

Health and care
- Protect NHS budget; up to £20bn efficiencies reinvested in care; no top‑down NHS reorganisation.
- Patient guarantees: 18‑week treatment or funded private; cancer test results within one week; health checks 40–74; evening/weekend GP choice; more care at home; access to psychological therapy.
- National Care Service: from 2011 free home care for greatest needs; from 2014 cap residential care costs after two years; towards universal care post‑2015.

Communities, safety, immigration
- Maintain police/PCSO numbers; neighbourhood policing; performance report cards; take over failing forces.
- Earlier interventions for problem families; faster ASB action with right to injunctions; expand Community Payback.
- Use CCTV and DNA (retain six years for arrested not convicted); non‑compulsory ID scheme self‑financed.
- Immigration: points‑based control; no unskilled non‑EU migration; tougher English; earned citizenship; Migrant Impact Fund.

Culture and environment
- Olympics legacy; expand school and community sport; supporter trusts in football; protect pubs and post offices; free museums; BBC independence.
- Green plan: about 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020 (renewables, nuclear, CCS); 400,000 green jobs by 2015; Pay‑As‑You‑Save home insulation; smart meters; zero‑waste drive; protect Green Belt; expand woodland; fairer markets for farmers and a Supermarkets Ombudsman.

Political and constitutional reform
- Referenda on AV for Commons and a democratic Second Chamber; fixed‑term Parliaments; lobbying register; recall for MPs; free vote on votes at 16 after better citizenship education; stronger local government; open data and digital government.

Global and defence
- Afghanistan: train Afghan forces, political settlement, aid and governance reform.
- Strategic Defence Review; maintain nuclear deterrent; improved forces’ pay, housing, healthcare, veterans’ support (Forces Charter).
- Active EU leadership; 0.7% aid by 2013 in law; climate leadership; reform UN, IFIs, G8/G20, NATO; human rights and conflict prevention focus.
